memoryText: The fear of the LORD is the beginning of knowledge; fools despise wisdom and instruction.
readingInstruction: No new reading today. Read Proverbs 1:7 slowly, several times, and then say it from memory. Read the meditation and the week in review, and choose one of the three questions to write about, pray over, or share with someone.
memoryVerseMeditation:
This verse is the motto of the whole book of Proverbs, and it appears again in 9:10. Everything in the book rests on it.

“The fear of the LORD.” The word fear has two layers in the Bible. There is the awe that shakes us when we realize who God is, and there is the trust that keeps us coming to him. A child who loves and respects his father fears him in this sense: he takes him seriously and does not want to displease him. To fear the LORD is to live as though God is real, holy, good, and in charge.

“Is the beginning.” The word can mean either the first part or the chief part. Both are true. It is where wisdom starts, and it is what wisdom is made of. You cannot skip it and arrive at wisdom some other way.

“Of knowledge.” It is the starting point for knowing anything rightly. The world makes sense only if the one who made it is acknowledged. Apart from him, knowledge becomes fragmented, proud, or useless.

“Fools despise wisdom and instruction.” The fool is not one who lacks intelligence but one who rejects correction. He thinks he knows best. The contrast is between a person who bows to God and a person who bows to himself.

For the Christian, the fear of the LORD is not opposed to the love of God. It deepens as we see his holiness and his grace together at the cross. We fear him because he is holy, and we run to him because he is merciful. Pray this verse often, and ask God to give you a heart that fears him.
weekInReview: This week you began the wisdom books. You opened Proverbs and heard the father’s call to his son, with the fear of the LORD as the starting point. You read the anchor of the unit, Proverbs 3:5-6, which calls us to trust the LORD with all our heart and not to lean on our own understanding. You read the warnings about adultery, debt, and laziness, and the beautiful alternative of faithful love. In the Psalms you saw the glory of God in creation and in his word in Psalm 19, and began Psalm 119 with its longing to walk in God’s law. You ended the week with Wisdom’s own speech in Proverbs 8, where she stands beside God at creation. The week taught that wisdom starts with reverent trust in God, that his word guards the heart, and that Christ is the wisdom of God.
reflectionQuestions: Proverbs 3:5-6 asks us to trust the LORD with all our heart and not lean on our own understanding. Where are you leaning on your own understanding right now?
Proverbs 8 pictures Wisdom as present with God at creation, and the New Testament shows Christ as the wisdom of God. How does that change the way you think about seeking wisdom?
Psalm 119:11 says, “I have stored up your word in my heart, that I might not sin against you.” What is one practical way you can store up God’s word this week?
prayerPrompts: Tell God you want to begin knowing him with fear.
Thank him for Christ, the wisdom of God.
Rest, and ask him to guard your way with his word.
